title: Replacement wave: next-generation narrowbody demand arrives with the MAX/neo retirements
narrative: Demand for a new-generation narrowbody follows the retirement of today's 737 MAX and A320neo-family fleets. MAX/neo replacements are about 40 aircraft in 2037, about 330 in 2040 and about 800 a year from 2044. A new airplane that enters service before the wave wins share more slowly, because few airlines are replacing aircraft yet; one that enters service as the wave builds wins it at the full calibrated speed.

replacement_wave._source: Boeing Product Development draft, 'Driver of late 2030s entry-into-service timing', slide 7: MAX/neo replacements by year (Boeing proprietary). Values read off the stacked chart, about +/-20 aircraft a year.
replacement_wave._capture_rule: capture weight = floor + (1 - floor) x min(1, replacements / mean replacements 2044-2046); floor 0.4 (assumption: a new airplane still wins growth orders and older-generation replacements before the wave); held at the 2046 value after 2046.
drivers: Retirement timing: a critical mass of MAX/neos reaches retirement age in the mid-2030s; orders typically need 5+ years of lead time
Product lifecycle: limits on further MAX enhancements cap its competitiveness; key elements (engines, materials, systems) are maturing
Eroding market share and margin: continued A320-family improvements may erode MAX share; price pressure may erode margins
Competition: stay ahead of COMAC and other new competitors; risk of being leapfrogged on efficiency or capability
